name: decepticon-exactly-once-middleware-effect-e9ec
instr:
Decepticon cannot recover middleware effects exactly once across interruptions without suppressing new work. Add stable identities and durable local histories so middleware can reconcile external effects, while unchanged behavior remains when recovery is omitted.

Equivalent retries share identity. Recovered engagement and model transformations reproduce the same caller-visible request on equivalent retries, while engagements, threads, calls, operations, and redirected arguments remain distinct without persisting secrets, bound model objects, or mutable request instances. Atomic effect beginnings, completions, abandonments, and committed outcome updates give concurrent readers durable, deterministic histories. Preserve valid prefixes and distinguish fresh, incomplete, completed, abandoned, corrupt-tail, and scope-mismatched histories without inventing success. Local inspection needs no network access; absent journals are harmless.

Instrument every standard, wrapped, replaced, disabled, and plugin middleware without changing stack order or safety-critical slots. Synchronous and asynchronous success, failure, cancellation, and redirection must agree. Event logging, approvals, KG hydration, budget warnings, and sandbox notifications reconcile at their observable completion boundaries. Do not repeat completed work; keep incomplete work eligible. Newer graph revisions, output, and authoritative spend still apply, including hard caps.
